title: Oklahoma 13, Florida State 2: The 2000 National Championship Game
question: What was the score when Oklahoma won the 2000 national championship?
answer: Oklahoma beat Florida State 13-2 in the Orange Bowl on Jan. 3, 2001, finishing 13-0 and winning the BCS national title in Bob Stoops' second season as head coach.
summary: Oklahoma beat Florida State 13-2 in the Jan. 3, 2001 Orange Bowl to finish 13-0 and win the BCS title. Here is how the Sooners defense shut down the Seminoles.
body: Bob Stoops needed only two seasons to bring a national championship back to Norman. His 2000 Sooners went 12-0 in the regular season behind quarterback Josh Heupel and a fast, aggressive defense, and they earned a spot in the Orange Bowl to play Florida State for the BCS title.

The game turned into a defensive clinic. Tim Duncan kicked field goals in the first and third quarters for a 6-0 lead. In the fourth quarter Oklahoma forced a fumble deep in Seminoles territory, and Quentin Griffin finished the short drive with a 10-yard touchdown run that made it 13-0. Florida State's only points came on a safety with 55 seconds left after a high snap on an Oklahoma punt.

The defense never let Florida State reach the end zone. With about 10 minutes left and OU up 6-0, cornerback Derrick Strait knocked down a fourth-and-10 pass at the goal line. The Seminoles converted just one of 13 third downs all night, and Chris Weinke threw two interceptions. Linebacker Torrance Marshall was named the game's MVP, and the coverage plan Bob and Mike Stoops built to keep Weinke guessing earned plenty of credit.
Oklahoma finished 13-0 as the only unbeaten team in the country. It was the program's seventh national championship and its first since 1985.
